value.rationale: An isolated neighboring-pair annihilation bond is a natural quantum reaction trap. The theorem distinguishes certain guaranteed annihilations (same parity sites) from nonzero protected fractions for opposite parity initial pairs and computes all fractions exactly for an infinite arithmetic family. Its nonresonance requirement has a structural physical meaning, and the result is reusable as an exact localized two-particle loss benchmark, not simply a reformulation, trivial size increment, or arbitrary table cell. It makes no unsupported claim about finite-time capture or other models.
